descriptionChirho: A precious blue gemstone (likely lapis lazuli in ancient usage rather than modern corundum sapphire), prized for its beauty and used in jewelry, priestly breastplate settings, and metaphorical descriptions of divine glory and human beauty. All three clusters represent the same noun סַפִּיר in singular, plural, and prepositional forms -- purely grammatical variation. Cross-lingual evidence is consistent: Arabic يَاقُوت (yaqut, sapphire/precious stone), Swahili 'yakuti samawi' (blue sapphire/heavenly sapphire), Hindi नीलम/नीलमणि (nilam/nilamani, sapphire), Korean 청옥 (cheong-ok, blue jade/sapphire) and 사파이어 (sapaieo, sapphire loanword), Spanish 'zafiro' (sapphire). Found in Exod 24:10, 28:18, 39:11; Job 28:6,16; Song 5:14; Isa 54:11; Lam 4:7; Ezek 1:26, 10:1, 28:13.
